title: Iteration methods: forEach, map, filter, find, reduce
learningObjectives: Explain iteration methods: foreach, map, filter, find, reduce and process JavaScript collections correctly.

understand.concept: Array iteration methods process elements using callbacks. forEach performs an action for each element; map creates a transformed array; filter creates an array of matching elements; find returns the first matching element; reduce combines elements into an accumulated result.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the method that matches the task makes code clearer. map and filter return new arrays, while forEach is used for side effects and does not return a transformed array.
understand.analogy: Each method is a different way to work through a list: visit, transform, select, locate, or combine.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript array and object methods have defined mutation, iteration, and reference semantics.

explain.narrative: The methods create a doubled array, a filtered array, the first score at least 90, and the total score.

examples.explanation: The methods create a doubled array, a filtered array, the first score at least 90, and the total score.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the array or object values described.

practise.guidedTask: Use map, filter, find, and reduce on a lesson list. Explain which methods return new arrays and which return a single result.
practise.independentTask: Build a small collection-processing example using arrays and objects. Test empty collections, missing values, and mutation behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates or returns a new value.
Use clear object property names and deliberate copying.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Iteration methods: forEach, map, filter, find, reduce</title></head><body>
<script>const scores=[60,80,95];const doubled=scores.map(x=>x*2);const passed=scores.filter(x=>x>=70);const first=scores.find(x=>x>=90);const total=scores.reduce((sum,x)=>sum+x,0);console.log(doubled,passed,first,total);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which method creates a new array containing elements that pass a test?
questions.explanation: filter() returns a new array containing elements that pass the callback test.

questions.prompt: What should you check when using an array method?
options: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value

questions.answer: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
questions.explanation: Mutation behaviour matters when arrays are shared across application code.
